exposure: Delivery mode (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Peripheral immune profile (IL-1β and IL-10 concentrations)
cohort: 76 healthy young male university students (36 C-section delivered, 40 vaginally delivered)
finding: Young adults born by Cesarean section exhibit increased psychological vulnerability to acute stress and prolonged exam-related stress compared to those born vaginally.
mod_finding: This study found that young adults born by C-section exhibited increased psychological vulnerability to acute stress and a prolonged period of exam-related stress compared to those born vaginally.
